definition: the process by which a poorer area becomes wealthier as better-off residents move in
paraphrases: urban renewal that pushes out locals
example: Gentrification often raises local property values while forcing long-standing residents to leave.

definition: a residential area on the edge of a city
paraphrases: a residential area outside the centre
example: Many families move to a suburb in search of larger homes and safer streets.

definition: the growth of towns and cities as more people live and work in them
example: Rapid urbanisation has stretched the water and sewage systems of many developing cities.

definition: homes priced so that people on ordinary incomes can buy or rent them
example: Governments should invest in affordable housing so that essential workers can live near their jobs.

definition: a heavily built-up area of poor, overcrowded housing with few basic services
example: Millions of children grow up in a slum without access to clean water or proper schools.

definition: a very tall building with many floors
example: The skyline of the financial district is dominated by a cluster of glass skyscrapers.

definition: the basic systems and structures a city needs, such as roads, pipes and power lines
example: Ageing infrastructure makes it difficult for older cities to cope with sudden growth.

definition: a useful or pleasant facility provided in a place, such as a park or library
example: Residents of the new district enjoy easy access to local amenities including a library and a swimming pool.

definition: a person who travels regularly between home and work
paraphrases: a person who travels to the office
example: Each morning thousands of commuters arrive from the surrounding villages.

definition: used mainly for people to live in rather than for business
example: Planners kept the industrial units away from the residential streets to reduce noise.

definition: a person who pays rent to use a house or flat owned by someone else
example: A tenant usually has few rights if the building is sold to a new owner.

definition: a person who owns property and rents it to others
paraphrases: a property owner who lets homes
example: The landlord agreed to repair the heating system before the new tenants moved in.

definition: a loan taken out to buy a home, repaid over many years
example: Rising interest rates have made it harder for young couples to keep up with their mortgage.

definition: relating to the renting of property or goods
example: The rental market in the capital is so competitive that flats are often taken within a day.

definition: the improvement of a run-down area through new building and investment
example: The regeneration of the old docks turned a derelict site into a thriving cultural quarter.

definition: the process of rebuilding or reorganising an area for new uses
example: Critics argue that the redevelopment of the waterfront benefits investors rather than local people.

definition: the central part of a large city, often associated with social and economic problems
example: Investment in inner-city housing has helped to revive neighbourhoods that were once in decline.

definition: the uncontrolled spread of a city into surrounding countryside
paraphrases: the unplanned spread of a city
example: Urban sprawl swallows farmland and forces residents to depend on cars for every journey.

definition: a large urban area formed when several towns and cities have grown together
example: The Ruhr is a polycentric conurbation made up of many cities that have merged over time.

definition: a very large, busy city, usually a capital or major commercial centre
example: Tokyo is a vast metropolis where several million people travel through the same stations each day.

definition: containing people from many different countries and cultures
example: London's cosmopolitan character is reflected in its restaurants, markets and festivals.

definition: full of energy, life and activity
example: The district has become a vibrant place with galleries, cafes and live music venues.

definition: in very poor condition because of age or lack of repair
example: Many of the dilapidated tenements were pulled down to make way for modern flats.

definition: abandoned and in a state of disrepair
example: Artists have transformed a derelict warehouse into a studio and exhibition space.

definition: the condition of having no permanent place to live
example: Rising rents and low wages have contributed to a sharp increase in homelessness.

definition: the legal removal of a tenant from a property
example: Tenants who fall behind with the rent risk eviction within a matter of weeks.

definition: the division of land into areas where only certain types of building are permitted
example: Strict zoning prevents factories from being built beside family homes.

definition: to make a street or area for walkers only by banning vehicles
example: The council decided to pedestrianise the main shopping street to attract more visitors.

definition: having many floors, usually used of large buildings
example: High-rise flats make efficient use of scarce land but can leave residents feeling isolated.

definition: a part of a town where people live, with its own character
example: She grew up in a friendly neighbourhood where everyone knew each other by name.

definition: having strong, friendly relationships between members
example: In a close-knit community, neighbours often look after each other's children.

definition: homes provided at low rent by councils or charities for people on low incomes
collocations: a waiting list for social housing
example: Waiting lists for social housing have grown because few new homes are being built.

definition: a situation in which there are not enough homes for people who need them
example: A chronic housing shortage has pushed prices beyond the reach of first-time buyers.

definition: a person or company that buys land and builds or improves buildings to sell or rent
paraphrases: a builder of homes for profit
example: The property developer promised to include a number of low-cost flats in the scheme.

definition: a building or feature that is easy to recognise and is typical of a place
example: The old clock tower is a landmark that tourists use to find their way around the town.

definition: relating to the government of a town or city
example: Municipal authorities are responsible for rubbish collection, street lighting and public parks.

definition: the elected local body that runs a city or district
example: The council has promised to build a new leisure centre beside the river.

definition: to examine something thoroughly and make major improvements to it
example: The city plans to overhaul its drainage system before the next rainy season.

definition: uncomfortably small and crowded
example: Several students shared a cramped flat with only one bathroom.

definition: having plenty of room inside
example: The spacious apartment had large windows that let in a great deal of light.

definition: to move to a different place to live or operate
example: Hundreds of families had to relocate when the old district was cleared for a new motorway.

definition: to force people to leave the place where they live
example: Rising rents threaten to displace the artists who first made the area fashionable.

definition: extremely dirty and unpleasant, usually because of poverty
example: Reformers in the nineteenth century were shocked by the squalid conditions in industrial towns.

definition: a large old building divided into flats, especially in a poor part of a city
example: Whole families lived in a single room of a crowded tenement.

definition: an area of grass, trees or plants in a built-up place
example: Access to green space has been shown to improve the mental wellbeing of city dwellers.

definition: the activity of people in the streets of a city
example: Narrow pedestrian lanes help to create a street life that large avenues often lack.

definition: entertainment available in the evening, such as clubs, bars and shows
example: Students often choose a university in a city with plenty of nightlife.

definition: the central business area of a city
example: Office rents downtown are among the highest in the country.

definition: a central place where a lot of activity or business takes place
example: Singapore has become a financial hub linking markets in Asia, Europe and the Americas.

definition: a main road or public path used by many people
example: The old thoroughfare was lined with shops, theatres and coffee houses.

definition: a professional who designs how land and buildings in cities are used
example: An urban planner must balance the need for new homes with the protection of open space.

definition: suitable to live in
example: Inspectors declared the flats no longer habitable after the roof began to collapse.

definition: to repair and redecorate a building so that it is in good condition again
example: The theatre was refurbished at a cost of several million pounds.

definition: to pull down a building completely
example: Plans to demolish the historic market hall provoked angry protests.

definition: the act of pulling down a building
example: The demolition of the old tower blocks made way for a public garden.

definition: the buying and selling of houses, flats and land
collocations: a slump in the property market
example: A booming property market makes it difficult for young people to buy their first home.

definition: the amount of money needed to pay for basic things such as housing and food
example: The cost of living in major capitals has risen faster than wages in recent years.

definition: lacking the basic things needed for a decent life
example: Children in deprived areas often attend schools with fewer resources.

definition: a part of a city where one group of people lives, often in poor conditions
example: Racial segregation produced ghettos in which residents had limited access to jobs.

definition: an area whose people differ in culture or character from those around it
example: The old quarter is an enclave of traditional crafts surrounded by modern offices.

definition: the area around a city where many people live and travel into the city to work
example: House prices in the commuter belt have climbed as more people work from home part of the week.

definition: full of life and energy
example: The old town is lively in the evenings, when the cafes spill out onto the pavements.

definition: waste water and human waste carried away in drains
example: Untreated sewage was being discharged into the river that supplied the city's drinking water.

definition: basic services such as water, gas and electricity
example: The monthly rent includes all utilities, so tenants do not receive separate bills.

definition: small and closely arranged so that little space is wasted
example: A compact city keeps shops, schools and workplaces within walking distance of homes.

definition: combining homes, shops and offices in the same area or building
example: Mixed-use developments keep streets busy throughout the day and reduce the need to travel.

definition: a person who is walking rather than travelling in a vehicle
example: Every pedestrian in the old centre has to share narrow lanes with delivery vans.

definition: the outer surface of the top of a building
example: A rooftop garden can provide fresh vegetables in a city with very little ground space.

definition: a very tall building divided into many flats or offices
example: Many families were rehoused in a tower block built in the 1960s.

definition: not occupied or in use
example: Thousands of vacant properties could be converted into homes for those who need them.

definition: a group of houses or flats planned and built together
example: The housing estate was built in the 1950s to house workers from the nearby factories.

definition: a residential area enclosed by walls or fences with controlled entry
example: A gated community offers its residents security but can weaken ties with the wider town.

definition: the uncontrolled spread of a city into the surrounding countryside
example: Urban sprawl has swallowed farmland on the edges of many fast-growing cities.

definition: the movement of people and businesses from city centres to the suburbs
example: Post-war suburbanisation left many city centres with shrinking populations and empty shops.

definition: an area of open land around a city where building is restricted
example: Planners rejected the housing scheme because it would have been built on the green belt.
